entities.name: Aulus Hirtius
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Aulus Hirtius was a Roman consul and military writer who played a significant role in the Battle of Mutina in 42 BCE.

As consul, Hirtius was part of Mark Antony's forces, which clashed with those of Octavian (later known as Augustus) in a battle that would mark the beginning of the end of the Roman Republic.

Hirtius' writings on military strategy and tactics were influential in the ancient world, and his experiences as a soldier and statesman helped shape the course of Roman history.

Despite his importance, Hirtius' legacy is often overshadowed by that of his contemporaries, and he is now remembered primarily as a minor figure in the annals of Roman history.

The inscription 'Aulus Hirtius, son of Lucius, from Lanuvium, consul, censor, pontifex' found on a marble slab in the Roman Forum provides a poignant reminder of his once-prominent place in Roman society.
